title: Stained Glass Transform explores prompt privacy without fully local inference
friendlyTitle: A new method tries to hide your prompt from a cloud AI service
summary: A technical reproduction examines Stained Glass Transform, a method that moves tokenisation and embedding to the user’s device and sends learned, obfuscated embeddings to a hosted model. The experiment reproduced the approach directionally but did not reach the paper’s claimed privacy level within its limited training run.
friendlySummary: The method changes your prompt into scrambled number patterns on your own device before sending them to an AI model. A small experiment showed promise but did not fully match the original paper’s privacy result.
whyItMatters: Prompt privacy remains a major barrier for sensitive cloud-AI workflows. Obfuscated embeddings could offer a middle ground between plaintext APIs and expensive cryptographic or local alternatives, but the model-specific training and incomplete reproduction make this research—not a production guarantee.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This could one day help people use powerful online AI without sharing the exact words they typed. It is still research and should not yet be trusted with important private data.
